18 y\/o female with a complaint of shortness of breath."},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003EThis is an online e-log platform to discuss case scenario of a patient with their guardians permission.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI have been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of patient clinical data analysis to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations and come up with a diagnosis and treatment plan.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EChief Complaints\u003C\/u\u003E:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA 18 year old female who is a student, came to the casuality on 03.01.23 with chief complaints of:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- shortness of breath since 2days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- fever since 1 week\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E- pain and swelling in the perianal region since 10 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EHistory of present illness:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient was apparently asymptomatic 6 years ago.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003ECourse of events:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E6 years ago:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe went to a nearby hospital because of her weakness, polyuria, polydipsia, polyphagia, and weight loss; while there, her GRBS was high and she was diagnosed with diabetes; she then started using insulin injections.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EInjecction mixtard 20U - x- 15U.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn between due to raised sugar levels she develops abdominal pain and consults a doctor and takes fluids and high dose of insulin\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1 week ago:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient had swelling over analverge that started as 1x 1cms and increased to the current size of 4x 4 cms along with discharge of pus and mixed with blood.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAlong with it she had high grade fever associated with chills and rigors,therfore she consulted a local doctor and received antibiotics\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe had used those antibiotics for 5 days, later developed nausea as she was not on a proper diet.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETherefore she decreased her insulin dosage to 5u-5u on her own since 3 days and developed shortness of breath on rest since 2 days.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAs sob was increased, she got her Grbs checked at home and it was 480mg\/dl, was then taken to local hospital and was given injection ( not known).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESince today morning her sob was increased. She went to hospital and RBS being high, insulin14u HAI given and referred here for further management.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPast history:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of similar complaints of swelling in inner thighs and in gluteal region 1 year back as she has taken covid vaccine.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt that time she consulted local doctor and recieved antibiotics ( amoxiclav 625mg\/po\/bd for 5 days and also herbal medicine for swelling, on local application it got relieved.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot a k\/c\/o hypertension, Tb, asthma, epilepsy, thyroid disorders.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EMenstrual history:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAge of menarche: 13 years\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMenses: regular, 28 days cycle\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFlow increased associated with clots and pain\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPersonal history:\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiet: mixed\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAppetite: decreased\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBowel and bladder: regular\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESleep: adequate\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAddictions: no\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EFamily History:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHer father is a known case of diabetes since 16 years and he was using insulin mixtard 2 times daily\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EGeneral Examination :\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EDiscussion\u003C\/u\u003E:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiabetic\u0026nbsp; ketoacidosis(DKA) or diabetic coma is the most common complication in type 1 diabetes mellitus.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EQ.What are precipitating causes in Dka?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIt develops under two situations :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA. Undetected or undiagnosed type1 diabetic patient may present in the ketoacidosis for the first time.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EB. Patients of type 1\u0026nbsp; diabetes on treamtment with insulin mmay develop it under any stress or following an infection.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EInfection is most common precipitating cause in known diabetes\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn this patient the precipitating cause was peri anal abscess and poor glycemic control.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHow it is diagnosed?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIt is diagnosed as a combination of hyperglycemia, metabolic acidosis and ketonuria\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHow it is treated?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIt was treated by correcting the substantial hypovolemia by giving fluids @ 100ml\/hr.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHyperglycemia was treated by giving insulin (Human Actrapid injection) intravenously.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EElectrolyte imbalance like hypokalemia is corrected by inj kcl infusion.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;
